subtopics.name: Big Bang Theory
content: Leading scientific explanation for origin of universe; began ~13.8 billion years ago from a singularity
Hubble's Law (1929): galaxies moving apart at speeds proportional to distance, proving universe is expanding #imp
Georges Lemaitre first proposed 'primeval atom' theory in 1927
Fred Hoyle coined term 'Big Bang' in 1949 radio broadcast (originally to mock the theory)

subtopics.name: Galaxy
content: Universe contains ~2x10^11 galaxies with roughly equal stars in each
Three basic shapes: Spiral, Elliptical, Irregular #imp
Milky Way is a spiral galaxy, also called 'Akash Ganga'; contains ~400 billion stars #imp
Andromeda (Messier 31/M31) is nearest major galaxy to Milky Way #imp
Sirius (Dog Star) is brightest star in night sky; Proxima Centauri is closest star to Sun #imp
Neutron Star: ~30 km radius, very high density, formed from supernova remnant collapse
Pulsar: highly magnetized rotating neutron star; Asteroids: rock/dust fragments between Mars & Jupiter orbits

subtopics.name: PYQs – Universe & Galaxy
content: PYQ: Most popular argument on origin of universe = Big Bang Theory (Ans: A – SSC CHSL)
PYQ: Statements on black holes emitting X-rays / pulsars being rotating neutron stars = Only 2 correct (Ans: B – SSC CGL)

subtopics.name: Jupiter
content: Biggest planet of Solar System; gas giant, 11x bigger than Earth; 95 natural moons
Great Red Spot: anticyclonic storm existing 300+ years
4 Galilean moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) discovered by Galileo in 17th century #imp
Ganymede is largest satellite in Solar System; Europa may host subsurface ocean #imp
Shortest day in Solar System; gravity ~2.4x Earth's #imp

subtopics.name: Saturn
content: Second largest planet; least density in Solar System (less than water) #imp
7 rings made of ice, dust & rock; 274 confirmed moons (March 2025) - highest
Largest satellite: Titan; Enceladus & Titan considered 'ocean worlds' #imp
Last planet visible to naked eye; revolution period 29.5 years
NASA: rings disappearing at worst-case rate, could vanish in ~100 million years

subtopics.name: Mars
content: Red Planet due to iron oxide in soil #imp
Second smallest planet; atmosphere has CO2, NO2, inert gases
Two irregular moons: Phobos & Deimos
Distance from Sun: 142 million miles

subtopics.name: Venus
content: Brightest and hottest planet (475C); nicknamed 'Lucifer'; Earth's twin planet
Atmosphere: 97% CO2 with sulphuric acid clouds #imp
Retrograde rotation (east to west); longest day in Solar System (243 Earth days) #imp
Also called Morning/Evening Star; second planet from Sun

subtopics.name: Sun, Moon & Mercury
content: Sun: star of Solar System, ~150x10^6 km from Earth; light takes 8 min to reach Earth
Next nearest star to Earth: Alpha Centauri
Moon's diameter is 1/4 of Earth's; Perigee ~364000 km, Apogee ~406000 km
Mercury: fastest planet in orbital motion, ~47 km/sec

subtopics.name: Geostationary Satellite
content: Orbits Earth with 24-hour period, stays fixed over same equatorial spot
Altitude ~35,786 km above equator, moves in direction of Earth's rotation

The Coastal Plains

Landform percentages: Mountains ~10.7%, Hills ~18.5%, Plateaus ~27.7%, Plains ~43.1% #imp

subtopics.name: The Himalayas
content: Young fold mountains formed by collision of Indo-Australian Plate with Eurasian Plate
Natural boundary between Tibetan Plateau (north) and Indian Subcontinent (south)
Latitudinal divisions: Trans-Himalayas, Himalayan Ranges, Purvanchal (Eastern Hills)
Longitudinal divisions: Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal, Assam Himalayas

subtopics.name: Northern Plains
content: Also called Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain; world's largest alluvial plain
Formed by Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra river systems
Divided into 4 regions: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, Khadar
Bhabar: porous, foothills of Shiwaliks, not suitable for agriculture
Terai: south of Bhabar, fine alluvium, suitable for wheat, maize, rice, sugarcane
Khadar: new alluvium, fresh silt yearly, extensive cultivation
Bhangar: older alluvium, contains calcium carbonate nodules called 'Kankars'

subtopics.name: Valleys
content: Land between 2 mountains is called a valley
Kashmir Valley: between Peer Panjal & Greater Himalaya
Kullu Valley (HP): between Dhauladhar & Greater Himalaya
Kangra Valley (HP): between Nagtibba & Greater Himalaya
Kathmandu Valley: between Mahabharat & Greater Himalaya

subtopics.name: Water Divide
content: Upland separating two drainage basins; e.g., Ambala on water divide between Indus & Ganga
Western Ghats are principal water divide of Peninsular India #imp
Separates east-flowing Peninsular rivers from west-flowing Konkan/Malabar rivers

subtopics.name: The Indian Desert (Thar Desert)
content: Located west of Aravalli Hills, mainly in Rajasthan; also called Marusthali #imp
Aravalli acts as barrier blocking monsoon winds from reaching desert
Average annual rainfall below 150 mm; some areas below 100 mm
Luni is the only large river; streams disappear into sand before reaching sea
Barchans (crescent dunes) dominant; longitudinal dunes near Indo-Pak border; Jaisalmer has barchan groups #imp

subtopics.name: Deccan & Other Plateaus
content: Deccan Plateau: triangular landmass south of Narmada river
Separated from Chotanagpur Plateau by a geological fault
Black soil (Deccan Trap) of volcanic origin, suitable for cotton & sugarcane
Aravalli Hills: highly eroded, extend Gujarat to Delhi (SW-NE direction)
NE extension includes Garo, Khasi, Jaintia Hills, geologically linked to Chotanagpur Plateau
Divided broadly into Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats

subtopics.name: Coastal Plains
content: East Coastal Plain: Ganga Delta to Kanyakumari; broader than west coast; includes Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri deltas
Famous lagoons: Chilika (south of Mahanadi delta, 75 km long), Pulicat (north of Chennai), Kollur (between Godavari-Krishna deltas)
West Coastal Plain: Rann of Kutch to Kanyakumari; narrower due to Western Ghats running close to Arabian Sea
Konkan coast: Daman to Goa (~500 km); Karnataka coast: Goa to Mangalore; Malabar coast: Mangalore to Kanyakumari (wider)

Contains ozone layer; dry, ideal for aviation #imp

subtopics.name: Troposphere Details
content: Lowest layer; begins at surface, rises 8 km (poles) to 18 km (equator)
Temperature inversion: atmospheric temp increases with altitude, reversing normal trend #imp
Normal lapse rate: temperature drops 1C per 165 m of height gained
Tropopause is boundary between troposphere and stratosphere; weather disturbances don't cross it #imp

subtopics.name: Important Concepts
content: Water Divide: An upland separating two drainage basins; e.g. Ambala lies on the water divide between the Indus and Ganga river systems. #imp
Western Ghats act as the main water divide of Peninsular India, separating east-flowing rivers from west-flowing Konkan/Malabar rivers. #imp
Himalayan River Systems: Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems. #imp
Ancient Indo-Brahma River is believed to have split into three major drainage systems over time; Ganga and its Himalayan tributaries represent the central drainage system.

table.notes: One of the three major Himalayan river systems
Originates in the Himalayas; forms Sundarbans delta with Brahmaputra #imp
Known as Red River; world's largest river island (Majuli) lies on it #imp
Forms delta in eastern coastal plains; longest peninsular river #imp
Flows parallel to Tapi; west-flowing river #imp

subtopics.name: Brahmaputra River
content: Also called the Red River. #imp
Origin: Chomayungdung Glacier (Tibet) near Mansarovar Lake. #imp
Known as Tsangpo in Tibet, Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, Brahmaputra in India and Jamuna in Bangladesh. #imp
Flows through Tibet, Bhutan, India and Bangladesh. #imp
Joins Ganga in Bangladesh to form Padma, later Meghna before entering the Bay of Bengal.
Majuli (Assam) is the world's biggest river island, located on the Brahmaputra. #imp
Sundarbans formed by Ganga and Brahmaputra is the world's biggest delta. #imp

subtopics.name: River Landforms
content: Meandering is formed by lateral erosion in flat terrain; outer bank erodes while inner bank deposits sediments. #imp
Oxbow lakes are formed when the neck of a meander loop is cut off by erosion. #imp
Important erosional landforms: V-shaped Valley, Gorge, Waterfall, Potholes and Meanders. #imp

subtopics.name: Exam Highlights
content: Jim Corbett is India's first National Park (1936). #imp
Kaziranga is famous for the One-horned Rhinoceros. #imp
Gir National Park is the only natural habitat of Asiatic Lions. #imp
Sundarbans National Park is famous for Mangrove forests and Royal Bengal Tigers. #imp
Manas and Kaziranga are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Assam. #imp
Bandipur is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
Periyar is famous for its Tiger Reserve and Periyar Lake.
Silent Valley is a biodiversity hotspot of tropical evergreen forests.
